correctness.rationale: All m≥9: an explicit (22,15,12), quota 60.5 class-symmetric rule misclassifies exactly C(m,3) original losing coalitions; an exact four-profile contradiction proves this is symmetry-optimal. For unrestricted nonnegative weights, a balanced multiset of 60 winning and 59 losing coalitions has equal incidence vectors and therefore at least one classification error for every injection into larger classes. Averaging gives 60 e_A/M +20e_1/B1 +15e_2/B2 +24e_3/B3≥1; coefficient comparisons for m≥9 yield e≥C(m,3)/20. Nonpositive quotas are handled separately. Every case has explicit finite or analytic justification. check.py passed 56 finite small profiles, 3,575,656 class-profile evaluations, 294,912 labeled coalitions and 300 relabeling certificate checks. Computation does not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The exact three-class game, the C-complete property, and the normalized weight-excess 1/(47m) are explicitly existing results (Einy–Haimanko Definition 17, Proposition 18, Appendix 8.7). The newly proved quantity is the minimum proportion of incorrectly labeled coalitions: Θ(m^3/8^m), with an exact class-symmetric optimum and a 60-to-59 incidence obstruction yielding an unrestricted lower bound. The primary paper Section 6 supplies only a general O(m^(-1/2)) upper bound for this parameter; it does not establish this sharp family-level order. Search cannot exclude all unpublished or unindexed equivalences.

value.rationale: The outlier/misclassification measure is independently motivated as a key distance-from-weightedness invariant in Einy–Haimanko Section 6 and in weightedness-measure literature. For their flagship asymptotically nonweighted family, this result identifies the sharp exponential-polynomial scale, strongly separating the two measures and showing a symmetry-constrained optimum. The finite trade certificate reveals why asymmetric weighting cannot make errors arbitrarily rarer in polynomial order. This is a natural complete asymptotic order for a previously unquantified invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice.
